testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When starting from a stop, what should happen?

options.text: A vehicle should shift to the right.
A vehicle should be put into third gear.
A vehicle should not roll back.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle should not roll back.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Press on and try to finish the trip.

questions.explanation: The only effective way to deal with drowsiness is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help temporarily, but they do not keep you truly alert. You will be even more tired when these drugs wear off.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you suspect a problem.

questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic around you and check for problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: How much water on a road is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water instead. It does not take much water on the road for this to occur.

questions.question: What endorsement test must you pass to transport hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly, especially when turning, changing lanes, merging, and doing tight maneuvers. Looking at fuel prices is not a driving task that requires mirror checks.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, what should they be?
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and that they are tight and secure. Clean them if they are dirty.

questions.question: When operating a truck that requires a CDL, what about seat belts?

options.text: You are never required to wear a seat belt.
You must wear one only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear one only if driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must always wear your seat belt while operating a commercial vehicle. The driver's seat must have a seat belt.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator helps prevent ice from forming in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is most common at night because people are naturally less alert during their normal sleep hours. Take precautions to prevent fatigue if you must drive at night.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a serious traffic violation?
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include excessive speeding, reckless driving, driving a commercial vehicle without a valid license, following too closely, and improper lane use. Multiple serious violations can result in losing your driving privileges.

questions.question: If you do not get an air brakes endorsement, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
You can only drive a vehicle with air brakes within your state.
You can only drive a vehicle with air brakes between states.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: To drive a commercial vehicle with air brakes, you must pass the air brakes knowledge test and use a vehicle with air brakes for your skills test.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: What happens when you travel downhill?

options.text: You travel at the same speed as on flat ground.
You will likely swerve to the right.

questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle speed up when going downhill. Slow down before you start going downhill to avoid overusing your brakes.

questions.question: What is the problem with an underloaded front axle?

options.text: It is needed for smooth steering.
It is encouraged because front axles are usually weaker than other axles.

questions.explanation: An underloaded front axle can make it hard to safely steer your vehicle. Balance your cargo weight properly.

questions.question: When checking a cargo lift on your vehicle, what should you look for?

options.text: That the lift is not leaking.
That the lift is fully extended.
That the lift is the correct color.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: Check for leaks, damage, or missing parts on your cargo lift. The lift must be fully closed and locked in place.

questions.question: Before you get to your vehicle, what should you check?

options.text: That the vehicle is shinier than others.
That the vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
That there are no puddles under the vehicle showing a leak.
That the vehicle is parked correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: That there are no puddles under the vehicle showing a leak.
questions.explanation: Look at your vehicle's condition before starting your inspection. Check for damage or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Check around the vehicle for safety hazards like other vehicles, people, or low branches.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, how should you use your brakes?

options.text: Keep the brakes pressed the entire way down.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, release them for a few seconds, then repeat.
Use the brakes only at the bottom of the hill.
Press the brake pedal with steady pressure the entire way down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, release them for a few seconds, then repeat.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use your brakes to help your engine slow you down. Apply brakes just enough to slow down, then release them once you are about 5 mph below your safe speed. Repeat this pattern.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and oil that build up. Water and oil in the brake system can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving, but get the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely right away while you can still control the brakes. Check and repair the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood unless you must. You can use a fire extinguisher to spray foam through the louvers, radiator, or under the vehicle. If you are not sure what to do, wait for firefighters.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, what happens to your speed?

options.text: You will come to a stop.

questions.explanation: When driving downhill, gravity pulls your vehicle forward and causes your speed to increase.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when:

options.text: You are driving at very high speeds only.
You can hydroplane at speeds as low as 30 mph.
It happens most often when tire pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can hydroplane at speeds as low as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely to happen when tire pressure is too low or tire tread is worn.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the flames.
Aim at the ground about two feet away from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: When using a fire extinguisher, stay as far from the flames as possible and aim at the base of the fire.

questions.question: When transporting livestock, drivers should worry about:

options.text: The vehicle's weight shifting as the animals move.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's weight shifting as the animals move.
questions.explanation: Live animals lean during curves and move while being transported. This makes the weight distribution unstable. Driving with livestock requires extra care.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push in the clutch when the engine is almost idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is almost idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is almost idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch when the engine is almost idle.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal slowly and stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine is almost idle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not required safety equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have the right emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be fixed, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and load while keeping the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: After starting the engine, if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on, it means:

options.text: The ABS is not working correctly.
The ABS is not turned on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working correctly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should turn on when you start the engine and then turn off. If the light stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, which of the following do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: Check your engine compartment for: oil level, radiator coolant level and hose condition, power steering fluid level and hose condition, windshield washer fluid level, battery connections and fluid level, automatic transmission fluid level, and belt condition. Also check for leaks and damaged wiring. You do not check the fuel level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: When going downhill, how can you use less braking?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. This helps your vehicle keep a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
The distance between the brake pedal's rest position and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
questions.explanation: Air brakes have a delay because air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is usually at least half a second of brake lag between when you press the pedal and when the brakes start working. Hydraulic brakes work instantly when you press the pedal.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you use the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which person should motorists NOT worry about as a distraction?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to the road. Watch for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers. A person sitting on a bench is not a distraction concern.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS stops working, how should you brake?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as hard as possible

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents brakes from locking up during hard stops. If ABS fails, your regular brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally without the ABS system.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do first?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant
Wait for the engine to cool down

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool down
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and wait for it to cool before adding coolant to a system without a recovery tank. Use gloves or a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between 3/4 of a second and one second. At 55 mph, you travel about 61 feet during this time.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for rear tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Rear tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on your vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: During a vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: Putting the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake
The vehicle touching a boundary line

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the skills test. Every encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Check your tires and rims before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What information must interstate carriers display on their commercial vehicles?
questions.explanation: Federal safety rules require carriers to display the legal name or trade name on each commercial vehicle in their fleet.

questions.question: Where can retreaded tires be used on a bus?

options.text: On the front of the bus.
On the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the rear of the bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They can only be used on the rear wheels.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, how does stopping distance change?

options.text: It is longer than on a normal surface.
It is shorter than on a normal surface.
It is about the same as on a normal surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is longer than on a normal surface.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces because the tires have less grip on the road.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A person talking to someone in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Watch out for people who are not paying attention to traffic. Be careful around drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and construction workers.

questions.question: Rough acceleration while driving is:
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.question: If brakes overheat while going downhill, they may:
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes causes them to overheat and lose stopping power. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used on rear tires only.
Yes, if carrying a light load.

questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: When you park and leave your vehicle, should you use the parking brake?

options.text: No, it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parked. However, do not use it if the brakes are very hot or if the brakes are wet and it is freezing outside.

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by:
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds the spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.
